items.name: ISO 42001
items.description: AI management system — international standard for AI governance

sections.text: Understanding the organisation and its context

requirements.text: Identify the internal and external matters that shape the AI management system and affect what it is meant to achieve.
requirements.rationale: Understanding context ensures the AIS addresses relevant risks and opportunities.

controls.description: Conduct an annual analysis of internal/external context factors affecting AI governance; document and review at management review.

requirements.text: Senior leadership must own the AI management system: set and communicate the AI policy, assign roles, and show the system is directed from the top.
requirements.rationale: Leadership commitment is foundational to effective AI governance.

controls.description: Secure board-level sponsorship of the AIS; include AI governance in the organisation's strategic planning and resource allocation.

requirements.text: Leadership must ensure the organisation sets AI policy and measurable AI objectives that fit what the business is actually trying to do.
requirements.rationale: AI policy must align with business strategy to be effective.

controls.description: Maintain a written AI policy approved by top management; establish measurable AI objectives; review annually.

sections.text: Actions to address risks and opportunities

requirements.text: Before planning changes to the AIS, weigh the context issues (4.1) and interested-party requirements (4.2) and decide which risks and opportunities must be acted on.
requirements.rationale: Risk-based planning ensures proactive rather than reactive AI governance.

controls.description: Maintain a risk register for AI-related risks; perform risk assessments before deploying new AI systems; document mitigation strategies.

requirements.text: Set measurable AI objectives wherever AI activities are managed, and keep them reviewable.
requirements.rationale: Clear objectives enable measurable AI governance.

controls.description: Establish SMART AI objectives at department level; track progress quarterly; report to management.

requirements.text: Decide what people running AI work must be able to do, verify they can do it, and keep the evidence.
requirements.rationale: AI competence ensures proper system design, deployment, and monitoring.

controls.description: Define competency requirements for all AI-related roles; maintain training records; conduct annual skills assessments.

requirements.text: Plan, run and monitor the processes the AIS needs — including AI-specific risk and opportunity controls — and keep them under control.
requirements.rationale: Operational control ensures AI systems are managed throughout their lifecycle.

controls.description: Implement documented operational procedures for AI system lifecycle: design, development, testing, deployment, monitoring, decommissioning.

requirements.text: Put validation and verification into the AI lifecycle so systems behave as specified.
requirements.rationale: Validation ensures AI systems perform as intended.

controls.description: Establish validation protocols for all AI systems before deployment; conduct periodic re-validation; document results.

requirements.text: Define what to measure for AIS performance and conformity, how, when, and who does it.
requirements.rationale: Systematic monitoring ensures continuous compliance and performance.

controls.description: Define KPIs and KRIs for AI system performance; establish monitoring cadence (at minimum quarterly); assign monitoring responsibilities.

requirements.text: Review the AIS at planned intervals from the top to confirm it stays suitable, adequate and effective.
requirements.rationale: Management review ensures AIS remains suitable, adequate, and effective.

controls.description: Conduct formal management reviews of the AIS at least annually; document findings, decisions, and action items.

requirements.text: When AI governance fails to conform, react, correct, and stop it recurring.
requirements.rationale: Corrective action prevents recurrence of AI governance failures.

controls.description: Maintain a nonconformity and corrective action process for AI governance issues; track remediation to closure; report trends to management.
